title: How to Use a Cleaning Comb to Clear Herb Shears
meta_description: Learn how to clean herb scissors quickly using a cleaning comb. Follow our step‑by‑step guide to keep your five‑blade herb shears fresh and ready for cilantro,
html:
Keeping herb scissors in top shape is essential for fast, effortless chopping. If you’ve ever struggled with stuck bits of cilantro or stubborn basil fibers, you know that a simple clean can make all the difference. Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide on how to clean herb scissors using the handy cleaning comb that comes with the Herb Scissors – five‑blade shears designed to mince herbs in one snip.

Why a Cleaning Comb Is a Game Changer

The cleaning comb is more than a novelty; it’s a purpose‑built tool that reaches between the five blades where a fingertip can’t. The fine teeth of the comb lift trapped herb fibers, while the spaced teeth glide over the cutting edges without dulling them. Using the comb after every chopping session prevents buildup that can cause uneven cuts and bacterial growth.

Gather Your Supplies

Before you start, make sure you have these items within arm’s reach:

  • Herb Scissors (the five‑blade model)
  • The included cleaning comb
  • A small bowl of warm, soapy water
  • A soft, lint‑free cloth or paper towel
  • Optional: a few drops of food‑grade lemon juice for extra freshness

Having everything ready eliminates interruptions and keeps the cleaning process swift.

Step‑by‑Step: How to Clean Herb Scissors

Follow these five minutes to keep your shears performing like new:

  1. Rinse Immediately. After chopping, hold the scissors under running water. The water flushes loose herb fragments from the blades and the comb’s teeth.
  2. Soak the Blades. Submerge the scissors in the warm, soapy water for 30 seconds. Warm water loosens any stubborn bits that may be stuck between the blades.
  3. Use the Cleaning Comb. While the scissors are still wet, insert the comb between the blades. Gently pull the comb back and forth several times. The comb’s teeth will lift out any remaining fibers without scraping the cutting edges.
  4. Rinse Again. Run the scissors under clean water to wash away soap and loosened debris. Pay special attention to the area where the blades intersect.
  5. Dry Thoroughly. Pat the scissors dry with a lint‑free cloth. If you like a fresh scent, dab a drop of lemon juice on the blades before drying; the acid helps prevent oxidation.

That’s it—your Herb Scissors are ready for the next batch of cilantro, chives, or basil.

Maintenance Tips to Extend Blade Life

Even with regular cleaning, a few habits can keep your five‑blade herb shears sharper longer:

  • Avoid Hard Materials. Use the scissors only on herbs and soft vegetables. Cutting through tough stems or bones can bend the blades.
  • Store Dry. After cleaning, store the scissors in a dry drawer or on a magnetic strip. Moisture is the primary cause of rust on steel tools.
  • Spot‑Check for Nicks. Occasionally inspect the blades for tiny nicks. If you spot one, a light sharpening stone can restore the edge without professional service.

These small steps prevent the need for costly replacements and keep your cutting experience consistent.

When to Use the Cleaning Comb vs. a Brush

Many kitchen gadgets come with a brush for cleaning, but the comb is specifically engineered for herb scissors. The comb’s thin, spaced teeth navigate the narrow gaps between the five blades, whereas a brush can’t reach that deep and may even push debris further into the joint. Reserve a regular brush for larger tools like food processors; rely on the comb for your Herb Scissors to achieve a thorough clean.

Quick Troubleshooting

If you notice the scissors still feel sticky after a clean, try these fixes:

  • Vinegar Rinse. Soak the blades in a 1:1 mixture of white vinegar and water for two minutes, then rinse and dry.
  • Repeat the Comb Motion. Sometimes a second pass with the comb dislodges hidden fibers.
  • Check for Build‑Up at the Pivot. Use a cotton swab dipped in soapy water to clean the pivot point where the blades meet.

These remedies usually restore the smooth snip you expect from a high‑quality set of herb scissors.

FAQ

Can I put herb scissors in the dishwasher?

It’s best to avoid the dishwasher. The high heat and harsh detergents can dull the blades and damage the cleaning comb. Hand‑washing with the comb is quicker and gentler.

How often should I clean my herb scissors?

Ideally after every use. A quick rinse followed by a comb swipe takes less than a minute and prevents buildup that can affect flavor and hygiene.

Is the cleaning comb safe for other kitchen tools?

The comb works well for any multi‑blade instrument, such as pizza cutters or pastry shears. Just ensure the tool’s material is compatible with stainless steel; avoid using it on non‑metallic blades.
